summary: Assistance requested: stepwise deactivation and safe offramp for aggressive batching/caching/quant flags after tenant tail-latency increase
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealth Analytics reports a sharp rise in 95th/99th percentile tail latency for a subset of traffic after enabling an aggressive optimizer profile (KV prefetch + large async batching + quant profile q4f16). The increase began at ~2026-03-09T22:10 UTC and correlates with an internal optimizer rollout for the tenant.

Impact:
- Affected traffic: ~8% of requests from the customer’s production routes (models listed above).
- Symptoms: elevated p95 and p99 token latency, intermittent streaming disconnects for long-context sessions, and a modest increase in 5xx rate (~0.4% -> 1.6%).
- Business impact: BrightHealth reports degraded UX for clinical note summarization flows — user-facing timeouts observed, blocking an in-progress demo.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dedicated-cluster-bh-prod (us-west)
- Routing: tenant pinned to redwood-13b-q4f16-kv-prefetch; fallback configured to redwood-13b-q8 when overloaded
- Recent config change: optimizer profile "aggressive-prefetch-v2" rolled to 100% of tenant traffic at 2026-03-09T21:50 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed patterns):
1) Issue occurred under production load pattern: many long-context streaming requests (avg seq len 1024 tokens)
2) Tail latency grows after sustained 10–15 minutes of high concurrency from the tenant
3) Manual traffic split to fallback model reduces p99 but is not an acceptable long-term fix for customer accuracy requirements

Observed metrics & logs:
- APM traces: elevated server-side queue time at serving-runtime layer (queue spikes from ~2ms to ~18ms) and longer KV cache eviction counts
- GPU metrics: no sustained GPU saturation; peaks correlate with batching bursts
- Runtime logs: repeated messages indicating increased kv-prefetch eviction and occasional prefix-cache miss storms
- Console: spike in per-route throttling for that tenant immediately after rollout

Initial hypothesis:
- The combined effect of large async batching + KV prefetch is creating bursty micro-queues that push tail latency up under the tenant’s long-context patterns. Quant profile may change kernel execution paths and interact poorly with prefetch heuristics.

Immediate mitigations attempted by customer before ticket:
- Rolled traffic to fallback q8 variant for 30% of traffic (reduced p99 but impacted result quality)
- Temporarily reduced batch size via client-side setting (mitigates but not sustainable)

Requested outcome from Support/Eng:
1) A concise, ordered safe-offramp procedure to stepwise disable the aggressive flags for the tenant in production with minimal user impact (prefer per-tenant, per-route gates).
2) Recommendations for quick instrumentation checks to confirm stabilization after each step.
3) If safe, a suggested short-term conservative optimizer profile to switch the tenant to while we investigate deeper.

Attachments/links:
- Dashboard snapshot: https://console.redwood.company/dashboards/brighthealth/tail-latency-2026-03-09.png
- Trace example: https://traces.redwood.company/trace/4f9b-a1c3

2026-03-11 08:45 - Engineering (Marisol Vega): Noted that quant profile q4f16 may still cause kernel path variance; suggest keeping current quant but add a conservative batch size cap (max_tokens_per_batch) as a next safety knob.

investigation_notes: Snapshot taken before any toggles: snap-20260310-bh
Per-tenant queue time metric is the best early indicator; instrumented a new alert threshold at 200ms p95 for this tenant route
KV prefetch eviction counters increased by 320% post-rollout; suggests prefetch concurrency was higher than expected for long contexts
No single-node GPU OOMs or high utilization observed — issue is queuing/batching interaction rather than kernel saturation
resolution: In progress. Temporary safe profile recommended: conservative-prefetch-stable (kv-prefetch=false, async_batch_window_ms=30, max_tokens_per_batch=1024, quant_profile=q8f16 if customer can accept reduced compression). Steps performed: disabled kv-prefetch tenant-gate, verified p99 reduction. Next: apply batch-window reduction and cap tokens per batch with canary at 10% traffic then 50% then 100%.
next_steps: Present the written off-ramp checklist to customer and get scheduled window for full change
Apply async_batch_window_ms reduction with 10% canary for 15 minutes, observe p95/p99 and 5xx; escalate if regressions
If stable, promote to 50% -> 100% with 30-minute observation windows
Parallel: run longer tracing and kernel-level telemetry to evaluate interaction with q4f16; open engineering investigation ticket if anomalies persist
